title: Reproductive Comprehensive Set 1: Female Physiology - Ovarian Steroidogenesis (Short Answer)

questions.prompt: What is the fundamental chemical precursor for the synthesis of all ovarian steroid hormones including progesterone and estradiol?
Identify the specific ovarian cell type that expresses LH receptors and is responsible for the synthesis of androstenedione.
Which pituitary hormone stimulates the enzyme cholesterol desmolase in the theca interna cells during the first step of steroidogenesis?
According to the "two-cell theory" of steroidogenesis, which specific androgen diffuses from the theca cells into the granulosa cells?
Which anterior pituitary hormone is responsible for stimulating aromatase activity within the granulosa cells?
Name the enzyme found in granulosa cells that catalyzes the conversion of androstenedione to testosterone prior to the formation of estradiol.
Describe the unique distribution of FSH receptors within the adult ovary.
questions.modelAnswer: FSH receptors are located exclusively on the granulosa cells.

questions.prompt: How do rising levels of estradiol affect the density of FSH receptors in the granulosa cells of a growing follicle?
questions.modelAnswer: Estradiol up-regulates FSH receptors, increasing the sensitivity of the granulosa cells to FSH.

questions.prompt: During the follicular phase of the menstrual cycle, what is the primary feedback effect of estradiol on the secretion of FSH and LH?
questions.modelAnswer: Estradiol exerts negative feedback on the hypothalamus (GnRH) and the anterior pituitary (FSH/LH).

questions.prompt: Identify the specific threshold condition regarding estradiol concentration that must be met to trigger the preovulatory LH surge.
questions.modelAnswer: Estradiol levels must rise to at least 200 picograms per milliliter of plasma and be sustained for a sufficient duration.

questions.prompt: What is the mechanism of positive feedback by which estradiol initiates the ovulatory surge of gonadotropins at mid-cycle?
questions.modelAnswer: High levels of estradiol increase the sensitivity of the anterior pituitary to GnRH by up-regulating GnRH receptors.

questions.prompt: Which ovarian hormone dominates the feedback regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis during the luteal phase?
Describe the effect of progesterone on the uterine threshold to contractile stimuli during pregnancy.
questions.modelAnswer: Progesterone increases the uterine threshold to contractile stimuli, thereby maintaining uterine quiescence.

questions.prompt: Identify the non-steroidal hormone produced by granulosa cells that provides negative feedback specifically to inhibit FSH secretion.
What is the physiological role of activin in the regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis?
questions.modelAnswer: Activin stimulates the secretion of FSH from the anterior pituitary.

questions.prompt: In the systemic circulation, how are the majority of ovarian steroid hormones transported?
questions.modelAnswer: They are transported bound to plasma proteins (such as sex hormone-binding globulin and albumin).

questions.prompt: Explain why theca cells are unable to synthesize estradiol independently and must interact with granulosa cells.
questions.modelAnswer: Theca cells lack the enzyme aromatase, which is required to convert androgens into estrogens.

questions.prompt: What metabolic change occurs in the hypothalamic temperature-regulating center in response to progesterone secretion during the luteal phase?
questions.modelAnswer: Progesterone increases the hypothalamic set-point temperature, resulting in a rise in basal body temperature.
